Federated training under heterogeneity

Three clients, equal training sizes and optimizer budgets, four rounds, five seeds. Higher accuracy is better.

Global held-out accuracy

Worst-client validation accuracy

Statistical query disclosure under experiment-ID resets

90 matched synthetic populations, one predefined two-query attack, three minimum-count thresholds, four policy modes. Lower exact inference is better. This is not differential privacy.

Exact count inference across paired populations

The original history policy is vulnerable when the caller changes experiment ID. The principal-wide policy keeps the history across IDs; harmless repeated queries remained allowed in the tested scenarios.

Disclosure across observer privileges

Lower MSE means more accurate reconstruction. These are model-update attacks, not a cryptographic SecAgg+ run.

Five-seed model-update reconstruction

Joint aggregate-only, all-label oracle

Joint reconstruction covers 24 public digit images. The evaluator can match images without identifying the victim institution.

Output-only membership inference

New: Five independent models per distribution, identical sampled member/nonmember queries within each seed. Underlying training membership sets are not identical. All AUCs close to chance.
